manifest.name: @hayward/git
manifest.author: Hayward
manifest.description: Work with Git repositories: clone a project, switch or start a branch, then review, stage, commit, and push changes.

GIT_REPO_URL.description: The remote repository's clone URL. The scheme selects the transport: 'git@github.com:org/repo.git' or 'ssh://git@github.com/org/repo.git' for SSH, 'https://github.com/org/repo.git' for HTTP(S). When set, pins git_clone/git_push to this repo and any 'url' argument the LLM supplies to git_clone is ignored. When omitted, git_clone requires a 'url' argument at call time and git_push targets whatever 'origin' remote was recorded when git_clone ran.

GIT_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY.description: The SSH private key to authenticate with, in OpenSSH or PEM format (e.g. the contents of an id_ed25519 file). Required for git_clone/git_push against an SSH remote — there is no anonymous SSH auth. Not used at all by https:// or http:// remotes, which authenticate with GIT_HTTP_TOKEN instead. Paste it exactly as it appears in the key file, newlines included — the PEM/OpenSSH format is line-oriented, and a value with its newlines collapsed (e.g. from a single-line input) will fail to parse.

GIT_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY.description: The public key matching GIT_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY (e.g. the contents of an id_ed25519.pub file). Optional — libssh2 can derive the public key from the private key, but supplying it explicitly avoids that extra step.

GIT_SSH_PASSPHRASE.description: Passphrase for GIT_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY, if it's encrypted. Omit for an unencrypted key.

GIT_SSH_USERNAME.description: SSH username to authenticate as. Defaults to 'git' (the conventional git-over-SSH username on GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket) if omitted and the URL doesn't specify one.

GIT_SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS.description: Additional trusted SSH host keys, beyond the bundled github.com/gitlab.com/bitbucket.org entries — one 'hostname SHA256:<fingerprint>' pair per line, matching the format `ssh-keygen -lf` prints (e.g. from `ssh-keyscan -t ed25519 <host> | ssh-keygen -lf -`). Required for any other SSH host unless GIT_SSH_STRICT_HOST_KEY_CHECKING is disabled. Has no effect on https:// remotes, whose certificates the host's TLS stack verifies.

GIT_SSH_STRICT_HOST_KEY_CHECKING.description: Set to the literal string 'false' to accept any SSH host key, bypassing verification entirely. Risky (no protection against a MITM'd or spoofed host) — prefer adding the real host key to GIT_SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS instead. Any value other than 'false' (including unset) keeps strict checking on. SSH only: it cannot loosen (or tighten) HTTPS certificate verification, which the host performs.

GIT_HTTP_TOKEN.description: Access token for https:// and http:// remotes, e.g. a GitHub personal access token or a GitLab project token. Sent as an HTTP Basic Authorization header. Optional: public repositories clone over HTTPS with no credential configured. Ignored entirely by SSH remotes, which use GIT_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY.

GIT_HTTP_USERNAME.description: Username paired with GIT_HTTP_TOKEN in the Basic auth header. Defaults to 'git', which GitHub and GitLab both accept alongside a token; Bitbucket wants the real account name, which is what this is for.

GIT_HTTP_ALLOW_CLEARTEXT_CREDENTIALS.description: Set to the literal string 'true' to permit sending GIT_HTTP_TOKEN over a plain http:// (unencrypted) remote. Off by default: a token on an http:// URL would cross the network in the clear, so that combination fails with an explanatory error instead. Anonymous http:// cloning needs no opt-in and is unaffected.

tools.name: git_clone
tools.description: Clone a remote repository into the workspace root. Fails if the workspace already contains a repository. Accepts SSH remotes ('ssh://...', 'user@host:path') and HTTP(S) ones ('https://...', 'http://...'); the URL's scheme selects the transport, and credentials for it are configured on the collection.

url.description: The remote repository's clone URL — SSH ('git@github.com:org/repo.git', 'ssh://...') or HTTP(S) ('https://github.com/org/repo.git').

depth.description: Shallow-clone depth. Omit for a full clone.

branch.description: Branch to check out after cloning, as a plain name ('develop', not 'refs/heads/develop'). Omit for the remote's default branch. Fails if the remote has no branch by this name — it never falls back to the default.

tools.name: git_status
tools.description: Report the working-tree status. Without `filepath`, lists every changed file (added/modified/deleted, staged or not; '*'-prefixed when staged and unstaged disagree); with one, reports that file's status string.

filepath.description: Workspace-relative path to check. Omit to list every changed file.

tools.name: git_commit
tools.description: Commit everything currently staged. Author defaults to a generic 'agent' identity if not supplied.

tools.name: git_push
tools.description: Push the current branch to the 'origin' remote, over SSH or HTTP(S) as that remote's URL scheme selects.

tools.name: git_log
tools.description: List recent commits on the current branch (oid, message, author).

depth.description: Maximum number of commits to return. Defaults to 10.

tools.name: git_diff
tools.description: List which files changed between HEAD and the working tree (added/modified/deleted/renamed/typechange), each with a unified-diff patch for text files; binary files report binary:true instead.

tools.name: git_branch
tools.description: List branches, each with its name, tip commit, and whether it's the one currently checked out. Reports the current branch separately, or detached:true when HEAD isn't on a branch at all (commits would land on no branch, and git_push would have nothing to push). Read-only — use git_checkout to create a branch or switch to one.

remote.description: Include remote-tracking branches ('origin/main', marked remote:true) alongside local ones. Defaults to false, i.e. local branches only. These reflect the last fetch — after a shallow or single-branch clone the remote's other branches won't appear.

tools.name: git_checkout
tools.description: Switch the working tree to a branch, creating it first when `create` is set. Without `create`, a branch that exists only on the remote is checked out as a local branch tracking origin/<name>. Fails rather than overwriting if uncommitted changes conflict with the branch being switched to — commit or stage them first. git_push pushes whichever branch is current, so this is what decides where commits land.

branch.description: Branch to switch to, as a plain name ('feature/login'). An 'origin/' prefix is accepted and stripped — either form means the same local branch.

create.description: Create the branch before switching to it, like 'git checkout -b'. Fails if a local branch of that name already exists; call again without this to switch to it instead. Defaults to false.

start_point.description: With 'create', the commit the new branch starts from — a branch name, tag, or commit oid. Defaults to the current HEAD. Ignored without 'create'.
